newsitem.title: USA: Municipal contract changes head for CBOT okay.
newsitem.headline: Municipal contract changes head for CBOT okay.

text.p: After receiving minimal, but positive feedback on proposed changes to the municipal bond futures contract, a Chicago Board of Trade official said Monday he would submit the proposals for approval by the exchange.
Steve Sural, director of the CBOT's financial markets group, characterized the comments from contract users as minimal and "pretty much in line with what we're going to do."
Monday was the deadline for comments on changes the CBOT has floated over the past few month for the sluggish futures contract.

With those comments in hand, Sural said his department would submit the proposed changes to the CBOT's products and markets committee at its meeting later this month. If approved, the proposals would then be up for approval by the exchange's board at its December meeting, Sural said.
If the exchange gives the green light to the changes, they would then be submitted to the Commodity Futures and Trading Commission for its approval, Sural added.

One proposal calls for increasing the minimum size of bond issues in the Bond Buyer 40-bond municipal bond index underlying the contract to $75 million from $50 million. Other proposals would expand the evaluation time for determining whether or not to delete bonds from the index due to illiquidity to 20 days from the current 10 days, and allow deleted bonds to return to the index as long as they continue to meet index criteria.
Another proposed change would raise the minimum trade size on which a pricing broker prices a bond issue to $1 million from $100,000.
Sural said the proposed changes could be implemented in the first quarter of next year if all the approvals fall into place.
He said the exchange's proposal for an electronic system for displaying bids and asks for bonds in the municipal bond index will not be part of the package submitted to the exchange.
Instead, exchange staff is working to encourage development of the system, Sural said, adding that it could take awhile for such a system to be developed.
